101: The Other World's Books Depend on the Bean Counter by Yatsuki Wakatsu and Kazuki Irodori (Yen Press) is a fantasy romance about finding your place through honest work. Seiichi Kondo, an overworked accountant, is pulled into another world by a summoning meant for the high school girl beside him. Left with nothing to do, he takes a job in the kingdom's finance department and starts untangling its messy books. It's a cozy, slow-burn BL for readers who like competent leads and a little office drama.
102: .hack//G.U.+ by Tatsuya Hamazaki (Tokyopop) is a sci-fi action story set inside an online game. In The World R:2, a lawless online RPG, a player named Haseo hunts the mysterious player killer Tri-Edge, whose attack left his friend Shino in a coma in real life. Chasing rumors and rival guilds, he finds the game hides much stranger things. It's a good pick for fans of the .hack games and virtual-world adventures.
105: Forbidden Dance by Hinako Ashihara (Tokyopop) is a shojo romance and drama about finding your nerve again. Aya Fujii gave up ballet after a crushing setback, until she sees a performance by Cool, an all-male dance troupe, and its lead dancer Akira. Determined to dance with them, she pushes her way into the group, where not everyone wants her. It's a short, heartfelt series for readers who like performing-arts stories with a romance.
107: Full Metal Panic! Overload! by Shoji Gatoh (ADV) is a gag comedy spin-off of Full Metal Panic!. Sousuke Sagara is an elite teenage soldier assigned to protect high schooler Kaname Chidori, but he has no idea how normal school life works. His battlefield instincts turn every small problem into a military operation, and Kaname's paper fan is never far away. It's light, silly fun for fans who loved the series' school comedy side.
108: MeruPuri by Matsuri Hino (Viz Media) is a sweet fantasy romance with a magical twist. High schooler Airi Hoshina dreams of an ordinary, low-key romance, until Aram, a young prince from another world, comes through her mirror. Stuck in her world under a curse that turns him into a teenager whenever he's in the dark, he ends up living with Airi. It's a short, charming shojo series from the creator of Vampire Knight, good for readers who like gentle magic and romantic comedy.
110: Mobile Suit Gundam SEED by Masatsugu Iwase (Del Rey) is a sci-fi war story adapted from the anime. Kira Yamato is a student on a neutral space colony when ZAFT forces attack, and he ends up in the cockpit of the Strike, a new Earth Alliance mobile suit. On the other side of the battle is his childhood friend Athrun Zala. It's a fast-moving take on the series for readers who like giant robots and divided loyalties.
112: Sword Art Online Progressive by Reki Kawahara (Yen Press) is a sci-fi action series set inside a deadly virtual world. It retells the story of Aincrad from the very first floor, after ten thousand players learn that dying in the game means dying for real. Kirito, a skilled solo player, and Asuna, a determined newcomer, team up to clear the floating castle one floor at a time. It's a great fit for fans who want a slower, fuller version of the original arc.
113: After the Rain by Jun Mayuzuki (Vertical) is a quiet romance and drama about dreams put on hold. Akira Tachibana was a high school track star until an injury took her off the field. Now working part time at a family restaurant, she finds herself drawn to her manager, Masami Kondo, a 45-year-old divorced dad who once wanted to be a writer. It's a gentle, thoughtful story for readers who like reflective slice of life with soft, rainy-day art.
114: Gacha Gacha by Hiroyuki Tamakoshi (Del Rey) is a teen romantic comedy with some fan service. Kouhei Kurita has a crush on Kurara Kirishima, his class's sweet, serious honor student. Then he learns that a video game brought out a second personality in her, a wild, flirty girl called Alice who appears at the worst possible moments. Kouhei decides to keep her secret and help her out. It's goofy, fast-paced fun for fans of 2000s rom-coms.
115: Gambling Apocalypse Kaiji by Nobuyuki Fukumoto (Denpa) is a psychological thriller about debt, desperation, and high-stakes games. Kaiji Itou is drifting through life when he's stuck with a huge debt after co-signing a loan for a former coworker. A loan shark offers a way out: one night of gambling aboard a ship called Espoir. It's tense and wildly inventive, a strong pick for readers who like mind games and underdog stories.
120: My Androgynous Boyfriend by Tamekou (Seven Seas) is a sweet romantic comedy about a couple who don't fit the usual mold. Mei is a hardworking career woman, and her boyfriend Meguru loves makeup and fashion and is often the prettiest person in the room. Together they navigate everyday life, other people's assumptions, and what they really want from each other. It's a warm, affirming read for anyone who likes gentle couple stories.
122: Tegami Bachi: Letter Bee by Hiroyuki Asada (Viz Media) is a fantasy adventure set in a land that never sees true daylight. In Amberground, Letter Bees brave monster-filled roads to deliver mail and the hearts it carries. Young Lag Seeing meets Gauche Suede, a Bee assigned to deliver Lag himself as a package, and the trip inspires him to become a Letter Bee too. It's a moving, beautifully drawn series for readers who like heartfelt journeys.
123: Girls und Panzer (Seven Seas), based on the anime, is an action comedy about an unusual school sport. In this world, tank warfare, or tankery, is a traditional art for young women. Miho Nishizumi transfers to Oarai Girls High School to get away from it, but the student council drafts her to revive the school's tankery team anyway. It's a light, upbeat mix of friendship and detailed tank battles for fans of the anime and military hardware.
127: Goblin Slayer Side Story: Year One by Kumo Kagyu and Kento Sakaeda (Yen Press) is a dark fantasy action series that shows how the Goblin Slayer got his start. After goblins destroyed his home village, a young man registers as a lowly Porcelain-rank adventurer and takes only goblin quests, which everyone else thinks are beneath them. Stubborn and methodical, he learns through hard, brutal experience. It's a good pick for fans of the main series; expect violence.
129: My Hero Academia: Smash!! by Hirofumi Neda (Viz Media) is a gag comedy spin-off of My Hero Academia. Izuku Midoriya and his classmates in Class 1-A are back, but this time the big fights and dramatic moments get turned into quick, silly jokes. Short chapters poke fun at the characters' quirks, personalities, and the main story's best-known scenes. It's light, goofy fun for fans who already know the cast.
131: The Candidate for Goddess by Yukiru Sugisaki (Tokyopop) is a sci-fi mecha drama about young pilots in training. On Zion, the last planet where humans survive, giant robots called Ingrids defend against mysterious invaders known as Victim. Zero Enna arrives at the pilot academy hoping to become one of the few who can pilot them. It's a compact series for readers who like academy stories and giant robots.
134: Grand Guignol Orchestra by Kaori Yuki (Viz Media) is a gothic fantasy and horror story about music as a weapon. A plague has turned much of the population into Guignols, living puppets that attack people. A traveling orchestra led by Lucille, a singer with a beautiful voice and a sharp tongue, roams the land fighting them with sound. Lavish art and dark fairy-tale drama make it a good fit for fans of Angel Sanctuary or Godchild.
135: Grandmaster of Demonic Cultivation by Mo Xiang Tong Xiu (Seven Seas) is a xianxia fantasy, mystery, and romance. Wei Wuxian, the feared Yiling Patriarch, died hated by the cultivation world. Thirteen years later, he is pulled back to life in the body of a young man who gave up his soul to summon him for revenge. Soon he crosses paths with Lan Wangji, a rigid, righteous cultivator from his past. It's a sprawling story for readers who love mystery and slow-burn BL.
136: Grandmaster of Demonic Cultivation by Mo Xiang Tong Xiu (Seven Seas) is a full-color comic adaptation of the xianxia fantasy novel. Wei Wuxian, once the most feared cultivator alive, is brought back from the dead years later in the body of a young man seeking revenge. Back in a world that still hates his name, he's soon caught up in a new mystery alongside the stern Lan Wangji. It's a lovely way to experience the story for fans of the novel and the donghua.
137: The Demon Ororon by Hakase Mizuki (Tokyopop) is a dark fantasy romance. Chiaki, a lonely teenage girl, finds a wounded stranger and takes care of him, only to learn he is Ororon, the king of hell, who has walked away from his throne. Ororon decides to stay by her side and protect her, even as the forces of heaven and hell come after them both. It's a short, moody shojo series for readers who like brooding demons and fated love.
138: Gravitation by Maki Murakami (Tokyopop) is a comedy romance about chasing music stardom. Shuichi Shindo, lead singer of the up-and-coming band Bad Luck, has his lyrics dismissed by a cold, handsome stranger, who turns out to be romance novelist Eiri Yuki. Shuichi can't let it go, and his stubborn pursuit turns into a stormy relationship. It's loud, funny, and dramatic, a classic early BL pick for readers who like rock-star energy.
139: Gunsmith Cats Burst by Kenichi Sonoda (Dark Horse) is an action comedy about bounty hunting in Chicago. Rally Vincent runs a gun shop and works as a bounty hunter, backed up by her explosives-loving partner Minnie May. Each case brings car chases, shootouts, and plenty of attitude. It's a fun follow-up to Gunsmith Cats for readers who like detailed guns, classic cars, and tough, capable heroines.
140: Gunsmith Cats by Kenichi Sonoda (Dark Horse) is a fast, stylish action comedy set in Chicago. Rally Vincent, a sharpshooting young gun shop owner, takes bounty hunting jobs on the side with her friend Minnie May, a demolitions expert. Their cases tangle them up with drug dealers, mobsters, and dangerous rivals. With detailed cars and gunplay and a lot of humor, it's a classic for fans of 1990s action manga.
141: My-HiME by Hajime Yatate (Tokyopop) is an action comedy about a school full of secrets. Yuuichi Tate transfers to Fuka Academy and soon meets Mai Tokiha, one of the HiME, girls who can summon powerful beings called Childs to fight monsters known as Orphans. Before long, Yuuichi finds himself tied up in the HiME and their battles. It's a lively mix of school life, fan service, and fights for readers who enjoyed the anime.
144: Astra Lost in Space by Kenta Shinohara (Viz Media) is a sci-fi adventure about survival and trust. Nine students set off on a planet camp trip, only to be swallowed by a mysterious sphere of light and flung thousands of light-years from home. With an old spaceship and limited supplies, they must hop from planet to planet to get back, while wondering whether one of them is a saboteur. It's a tight, twisty story with plenty of heart.
145: Happy Happy Clover by Sayuri Tatsuyama (Viz Media) is a cheerful comedy adventure for younger readers. Clover is an energetic little bunny who lives in Crescent Forest with her friends. Whether she's exploring, playing tricks, or getting into trouble, every day brings something new. It's a sweet, gentle series with expressive art that works well for early readers and anyone who loves cute animal stories.
146: Happy Hustle High by Rie Takada (Viz Media) is a shojo romantic comedy with plenty of energy. Hanabi Oozora is a tomboy who loves sports and has no interest in being ladylike. When her all-girls school merges with a boys' school, she lands right in the path of Yasuaki, the cool, aloof student council president. It's a fun, fast read for fans of bickering couples and school comedies.
147: Attack on Titan by Hajime Isayama (Kodansha) is a dark fantasy action story about humanity's last stand. For a hundred years, what's left of humanity has lived behind enormous walls, safe from the giant man-eating Titans outside. When a colossal Titan breaks through, young Eren Yeager watches his home fall and vows to wipe out every Titan. This omnibus edition collects the series in bigger volumes, a good fit for readers who want to read it straight through.
148: Azumanga Daioh by Kiyohiko Azuma (ADV) is a laid-back comedy about the everyday lives of high school girls. Ten-year-old prodigy Chiyo skips ahead to high school, where she makes friends with dreamy Osaka, quiet Sakaki, loud Tomo, and level-headed Yomi, under their scatterbrained teacher Yukari. Told in four-panel comic strips, it follows them through classes, festivals, and summers. It's warm, funny, and a classic for slice-of-life fans.
151: Battle Angel Alita: Last Order by Yukito Kishiro (Kodansha) is a sci-fi action series that continues the story of Battle Angel Alita. Alita, a cyborg fighter, wakes up rebuilt by the eccentric genius Desty Nova and finds herself in Ketheres, a city in orbit high above Earth. Soon she's drawn into the Zenith of Things Tournament, where fighters from across the solar system compete. It's a dense, action-packed read for readers who finished the original series.
153: Hollow Fields by Madeleine Rosca (Seven Seas) is a gothic fantasy with a sense of humor. Young Lucy Snow ends up, by mistake, enrolled at Miss Weaver's Academy for the Scientifically Gifted and Ever So Slightly Dead. The school runs on strict rules, clockwork, and very strange teachers, and students who fail tend to disappear. It's a spooky, charming series for readers who like Tim Burton-style boarding school stories.
155: Oreimo by Tsukasa Fushimi (Dark Horse) is a comedy about siblings and secret hobbies. Kyosuke Kosaka barely talks to his younger sister Kirino, a stylish model and honor student who seems perfect. Then he discovers she's secretly a huge otaku with a stash of anime and games, and she makes him her reluctant confidant. It's a light, chatty comedy about fandom and family for readers who enjoyed the anime.
159: Paradise Kiss by Ai Yazawa (Tokyopop) is a stylish romance and drama about figuring out who you want to be. Yukari Hayasaka is a high school senior stuck studying for exams she doesn't care about, until a group of fashion students scouts her to model for their label, Paradise Kiss. Through them, and the charming, unpredictable designer George, she gets a glimpse of a life she never imagined. It's a classic for fans of Nana and grown-up shojo.
161: I've Been Killing Slimes for 300 Years and Maxed Out My Level by Kisetsu Morita (Yen Press) is a cozy fantasy comedy. After working herself to death at an office job, Azusa is reborn as an immortal witch and settles into a quiet life in the countryside. Three hundred years of killing slimes for spending money quietly raise her to the max level, and word gets out. Soon her peaceful home fills up with visitors, rivals, and new family. It's relaxed, sweet, and funny.
164: Peace Maker by Nanae Chrono (Tokyopop) is a historical action story set in late Edo-period Kyoto. Tetsunosuke Ichimura is a short, hot-tempered teenager who wants to join the Shinsengumi, the feared police force, to get strong enough to avenge his parents' murder. Taken on as a page, he grows close to the group's captains and learns what strength really costs. It's a mix of humor, swordplay, and tragedy for readers interested in samurai history.
169: Cactus's Secret by Nene Yukimori (Viz Media) is a sweet romantic comedy about a crush that just won't land. Miku Kobayashi likes her classmate Kyohei Fujioka, a prickly boy who seems completely oblivious. No matter how many times she tries to show her feelings, he misses the point, or does he? It's a quick, funny, heartwarming read for fans of awkward first love.
176: Jiu Jiu by Touya Tobina (Viz Media) is a shojo fantasy about a hunter and her loyal companions. Takamichi Akiba comes from a family of demon hunters and has been raised to be tough and practical. Her family gives her two wolf pups, called jiu jiu, as familiars, and they grow up fast, soon able to take the form of teenage boys. Raising them turns out to be more than she bargained for. It's a cute, offbeat series for fans of supernatural shojo.
179: Please Tell Me! Galko-chan by Kenya Suzuki (Seven Seas) is a short-chapter comedy about high school girls and their frank conversations. Galko looks like a flashy gyaru, and the rumors about her are wild, but she's actually kind, shy, and a little old-fashioned. With her friends Otako and Ojou, she trades questions about bodies and growing up that most girls wonder about but rarely ask. It's funny and good-natured, with some mild fan service.
180: Princess Princess by Mikiyo Tsuda (DMP) is a comedy set at an all-boys school with an unusual tradition. When Toru Kono transfers to Fujimori Academy, he learns that the cutest boys are chosen as Princesses, who dress up in frilly outfits to brighten campus life. He's quickly drafted alongside Yujiro and Mikoto, and the job comes with perks and headaches. It's a lighthearted series for readers who like school comedies with a touch of shonen-ai.
183: Tower of God by SIU (Webtoon) is a fantasy action story about climbing a mysterious tower. Twenty-Fifth Baam has spent his whole life alone in the dark, with only his friend Rachel for company. When Rachel enters the Tower to see the stars, Baam follows her inside, where every floor brings deadly tests and strange new allies. It's a sprawling, inventive adventure for readers who like puzzle-box worlds and big casts.
192: Ultra Maniac by Wataru Yoshizumi (Viz Media) is a lighthearted magical romantic comedy. Ayu Tateishi is the cool, popular girl at her middle school, but she has a soft spot for romance. Then she befriends Nina Sakura, a clumsy transfer student who turns out to be a witch-in-training from the Magic Kingdom. Nina's spells tend to backfire, and Ayu keeps ending up in the middle of them. It's sweet, short, and fun.
194: Kilala Princess by Rika Tanaka and Nao Kodaka (Tokyopop) is a magical adventure for younger readers. Kilala is an ordinary girl who loves Disney princesses. When she meets Rei, a mysterious boy searching for a princess who can save his kingdom, a magic tiara sends them into the worlds of Snow White, Cinderella, and others. Along the way, Kilala learns what it really takes to be a princess. It's a sweet pick for Disney fans.
